referenceComparison.01: The reference forms a broad dark forest boundary with irregular but coherent edge feathering; both arms remain separate trees over exposed olive terrain.
referenceComparison.02: Reference forest masses remain legible as volumes in a wide settlement view; neither arm achieves that tonal separation.
referenceComparison.03-04: Reference close ground treatment is earthy, restrained, and spatially varied; both arms show more uniform and visually noisy brown roadside stippling.
referenceComparison.05: The reference permits only small irregular warm-brown floor glimpses inside a predominantly deep canopy volume; both arms invert that hierarchy and let bright ground dominate.
referenceComparison.06-07: Reference treelines build layered dark boundaries behind readable settlement space; both arms remain thin and comparatively flat.
referenceComparison.08: The top-down reference forest reads as one charcoal or blue-green volume with soft organic openings; neither arm approaches that cohesion.
referenceComparison.09-10: The references preserve crisp roads and parcels through restrained vegetation and coherent shadows; both arms preserve basic readability but remain busier and less natural.

biggestRemainingGap: A continuous crown-density-driven shadowed woodland floor that suppresses the olive base into one deep forest volume, leaving only restrained irregular leaf-litter openings and feathering naturally before roads and parcels.
smallestNextImprovement: Make the connected dense-crown footprint visibly broader and darker at low frequency so frames 000 and 480 lose obvious olive holes, while retaining irregular leaf-litter openings, exact road and parcel clearance, and pop-free frames 276-279.
